sections.title: How does the Drake equation for love calculator work?
sections.html:
The Drake equation for love calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports number of potential partners (G) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the location, your attractiveness (fQ) and the social skills (fC)); then you type in the minimum age, the maximum age, the total population (N) and the age (fA).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

sections.title: The formula behind the Drake equation for love calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Number of potential partners (G)=((1 ÷ 100) × % you find attractive (fB) × social skills (fC) × location (fL) × gender (fG) × total population (N) × your attractiveness (fQ) × (location, gender, minimum age, maximum age) × (minimum age, maximum age) × (location, university educated))
Percentage chance of finding love=(((1 ÷ 100) × % you find attractive (fB) × social skills (fC) × location (fL) × gender (fG) × total population (N) × your attractiveness (fQ) × (location, gender, minimum age, maximum age) × (minimum age, maximum age) × (location, university educated)) ÷ (location (fL) × total population (N)))
Number of potential partners (G - customised)=((1 ÷ 100) × age (fA) × % you find attractive (fB) × social skills (fC) × location (fL) × single rate (fS) × university degree (fU) × gender (fG) × total population (N) × your attractiveness (fQ))
Percentage chance of finding love (customised)=(((1 ÷ 100) × age (fA) × % you find attractive (fB) × social skills (fC) × location (fL) × single rate (fS) × university degree (fU) × gender (fG) × total population (N) × your attractiveness (fQ)) ÷ (location (fL) × total population (N)))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • %, opening in percent

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Drake equation for love calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the minimum age and the maximum age — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Drake equation for love calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns number of potential partners (G), derived from the minimum age and the maximum age. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Drake equation for love calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the minimum age and the maximum age, which is 26 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter percentage chance of finding love in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Percentage chance of finding love opens in percent and the chip beside it offers 6 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (20 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports % you find attractive (fB) = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Drake equation for love calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
